OnUpgrade.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): STICKY KEYWORD FIXED AT THE SEAM, per binding rule 3 -- see creature_card_cmds/step52. `Card.downgrade` (cards/base.py) now deletes the instance-level shadow of every CardKeyword-backed attribute before re-running `_init_vars`, which is `DowngradeInternal`'s `_keywords = cardModel.GetKeywordsWithSources(KeywordSources.Local).ToHashSet()` (CardModel.cs:2143). The card file itself is UNCHANGED: the defect was never in `_on_upgrade`, which faithfully ports `AddKeyword`/`RemoveKeyword`, but in the rebuild that was supposed to undo it -- which is why a per-card `_init_vars` line would have been the wrong fix, needing to be repeated for every future card. `py audit/tools/card_probes.py downgrade` goes 5 of 203 -> **0 of 203**. Pinned by test/test_downgrade_rebuild.py::test_upgrade_then_downgrade_restores_the_keyword and by a pool-wide sweep over all seven keywords. NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: `AddKeyword(CardKeyword.Innate)` (HelloWorld.cs:27) maps to `self.innate = True`, which is correct at upgrade level 1. DOWNGRADE IS STICKY: `Card.downgrade` (cards/base.py:150-165) rebuilds by re-running `_init_vars` and re-applying upgrades, and `_init_vars` does not re-seed the flag, so the instance attribute written by `_on_upgrade` survives. C# `DowngradeInternal` rebuilds the whole keyword set from canonical (`_keywords = cardModel.GetKeywordsWithSources(KeywordSources.Local).ToHashSet()`, CardModel.cs:2143). EXECUTED: `py audit/tools/card_probes.py downgrade` lists this card among the 5 of 203 that do not restore. LIVE -- `downgrade()` is reachable from `events/reflections.py:40`, `events/welcome_to_wongos.py:90` (both registered in `events/__init__.py`) and `powers.py:3171` (DampenPower). Same mechanism and same verdict as card/aggression's and card/apparition's OnUpgrade entries (rule 3). The fix is one line: re-seed the flag in `_init_vars`, as card/anointed, card/discovery, card/entropy and card/gold_axe all do. Observable: a downgraded Hello World still starts every combat in the opening hand in the sim; in the game it does not.
